title: Preparation for the Temple
overview: 1 Chronicles 22 details King David’s preparations for the construction of the temple, a sacred project that would be fulfilled by his son Solomon. Although David desired to build the house of the LORD himself, God’s word forbade him due to his history of warfare and bloodshed. Instead, David gathers materials, skilled laborers, and commands the leaders of Israel to support Solomon in this divine task. This chapter highlights the importance of obedience to God’s timing and instructions, the passing of spiritual responsibility from one generation to the next, and the necessity of wisdom and courage in fulfilling God’s purposes. It serves as a pivotal moment in Israel’s history, setting the stage for the temple’s construction and the establishment of Solomon’s reign.
structure:
**Verses 1-5: David’s Preparations for the Temple.** David identifies the sacred site and organizes labor and materials, including stones, iron, brass, and cedar wood, emphasizing the grandeur required for God’s house. He acknowledges Solomon’s youth and begins preparations for the temple’s construction.

**Verses 6-10: David Charges Solomon.** David summons Solomon and reveals God’s command that Solomon, not David, will build the temple. He explains the divine reason for this—David’s history of bloodshed—and prophesies Solomon’s peaceful reign and God’s covenant with him.

**Verses 11-16: Exhortation and Provision.** David encourages Solomon to seek the LORD’s wisdom and understanding to govern Israel and build the temple successfully. He details the abundant resources and skilled workers already prepared for the task.

**Verses 17-19: David Commands Support for Solomon.** David instructs the princes of Israel to assist Solomon, reminding them of God’s deliverance and urging wholehearted commitment to building the sanctuary and bringing the ark and holy vessels into the temple.

keyVerses.text: But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, Thou hast shed blood abundantly, and hast made great wars: thou shalt not build an house unto my name, because thou hast shed much blood upon the earth in my sight.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals God’s sovereign judgment and plan, explaining why David, despite his desire, is not permitted to build the temple. It underscores the holiness required for this sacred task and God’s control over His purposes.

keyVerses.text: He shall build an house for my name; and he shall be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.
keyVerses.significance: This prophecy affirms Solomon’s divine appointment and the everlasting nature of his kingdom, highlighting God’s covenant relationship with Solomon and the significance of the temple as a symbol of God’s presence.

keyVerses.text: Only the LORD give thee wisdom and understanding, and give thee charge concerning Israel, that thou mayest keep the law of the LORD thy God.
keyVerses.significance: David’s prayer for Solomon emphasizes the necessity of divine wisdom and obedience to God’s law for successful leadership and temple construction, linking spiritual insight with practical governance.

keyVerses.text: Now, behold, in my trouble I have prepared for the house of the LORD an hundred thousand talents of gold, and a thousand thousand talents of silver; and of brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance: timber also and stone have I prepared; and thou mayest add thereto.
keyVerses.significance: This verse demonstrates David’s dedication and foresight in gathering vast resources, showing the importance of preparation and stewardship in fulfilling God’s work.

keyVerses.text: Now set your heart and your soul to seek the LORD your God; arise therefore, and build ye the sanctuary of the LORD God, to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and the holy vessels of God, into the house that is to be built to the name of the LORD.
keyVerses.significance: David’s final exhortation calls for wholehearted devotion to God and the temple project, emphasizing the spiritual focus and reverence required in serving the LORD.

characters.name: David
characters.description: King of Israel who initiates the preparations for the temple. Though he desires to build the house of the LORD, God forbids him due to his violent past. David’s role is foundational as he gathers materials, organizes labor, and charges Solomon to complete the work.

characters.name: Solomon
characters.description: David’s son and successor, chosen by God to build the temple. Solomon is described as young and tender, but divinely appointed to reign in peace and construct the house of God, continuing David’s legacy under God’s guidance.

characters.name: The LORD God
characters.description: The sovereign God who directs the building of His temple. He communicates His will to David, forbidding him from building due to bloodshed and promising Solomon rest and peace. God’s presence and covenant are central to the chapter.

characters.name: Princes of Israel
characters.description: The leaders of Israel whom David commands to support Solomon in building the temple. Their cooperation reflects the unity and communal responsibility in fulfilling God’s purposes.

themes.description: God’s control over who builds the temple and when is clear in this chapter. David’s exclusion and Solomon’s appointment demonstrate that God’s plans unfold according to His perfect wisdom and timing.
David’s extensive gathering of materials and skilled workers highlights the importance of diligent preparation and wise stewardship in accomplishing God’s work.
The call for Solomon to seek wisdom and keep God’s law underscores the necessity of spiritual insight and obedience for leadership and service to God.
The passing of the temple-building task from David to Solomon illustrates the biblical principle of passing spiritual responsibilities from one generation to the next.
God’s promise of rest and peace to Solomon contrasts with David’s life of warfare, emphasizing the blessings of righteous leadership and God’s covenantal faithfulness.

historicalContext: This chapter is set during the late reign of King David, around the 10th century BC, in the ancient kingdom of Israel. Jerusalem had been established as the political and religious center, and David’s desire to build a permanent temple reflected the need for a central place of worship for the nation. The political situation involved consolidating Israel’s territories and ensuring stability after years of conflict. The involvement of Zidonians and Tyrians in providing cedar wood indicates international trade and alliances. The cultural context includes the importance of temple worship in Israelite religion, with strict adherence to God’s commands regarding sacred spaces and leadership.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes God’s sovereign election and providence in choosing Solomon to build the temple, highlighting the importance of obedience to God’s revealed will and the covenantal promises made to David’s lineage.

Dispensationalists see this chapter as part of God’s unfolding plan for Israel, with the temple representing a literal fulfillment of God’s promises to David’s dynasty, foreshadowing the millennial kingdom where temple worship will be restored.

Early Church Fathers often interpreted Solomon’s temple as a type of Christ and the Church, with the building representing the spiritual temple of God. David’s preparations are seen as prefiguring the work of Christ preparing a place for His people.

crossReferences.connection: God’s promise to David that his son will build the temple and establish an everlasting kingdom is first given here, directly related to the message in 1 Chronicles 22.
The call for Solomon to seek wisdom and understanding aligns with the biblical principle of trusting in the LORD for guidance, as emphasized in Proverbs.
The command to build a sanctuary for God’s presence echoes the original instructions for the tabernacle, showing continuity in God’s desire for a dwelling place among His people.
The emphasis on the LORD’s blessing for success in building the temple reflects the truth that without God’s help, human efforts are in vain.
The comparison of Jesus to Moses and the house built by God connects to the temple’s significance as God’s house and the fulfillment of God’s promises.

application: Commit to preparing diligently and prayerfully for the tasks God has given you, recognizing the importance of stewardship and readiness.
Seek God’s wisdom and understanding daily, especially when facing leadership or significant responsibilities.
Trust in God’s sovereign timing and plan, even when your desires differ from His immediate will.
Encourage and support others in their God-given callings, fostering unity and cooperation within the body of Christ.
Remember that obedience to God’s law and commands leads to blessing and success in His work.
Set your heart and soul to seek the LORD earnestly, prioritizing Him above all in your life and service.
conclusion: 1 Chronicles 22 stands as a powerful testament to God’s sovereign plan and the importance of faithful preparation in fulfilling His purposes. David’s example teaches believers to honor God’s timing, seek divine wisdom, and steward resources wisely. The chapter’s themes of obedience, generational responsibility, and peace through God’s covenant encourage Christians to trust God fully and actively participate in His work. As Solomon is charged to build the temple, believers today are reminded to build their lives and communities on God’s foundation with courage and devotion.
timeline: c. 1000 BC - Late Reign of King David, Preparations for the Temple

outline.heading: David’s Preparations for the Temple
outline.description: David identifies the temple site, organizes labor including foreign workers, and gathers abundant materials like iron, brass, and cedar wood, preparing for a magnificent house for the LORD.

outline.heading: David Charges Solomon to Build the Temple
outline.description: David calls Solomon, explains God’s prohibition against him building the temple due to his bloodshed, and prophesies Solomon’s peaceful reign and divine appointment to build the house of God.

outline.heading: Exhortation for Wisdom and Provision
outline.description: David prays for Solomon’s wisdom and understanding to govern Israel and fulfill the temple project, detailing the vast resources and skilled craftsmen already prepared.

outline.heading: Command to Support Solomon
outline.description: David commands the princes of Israel to assist Solomon, reminding them of God’s deliverance and urging wholehearted dedication to building the sanctuary and bringing the ark into the temple.
